title: 2606.28570v1 (1)
universal_lens: A mathematical lens unifying coaching intelligence via agent-based multimodal fusion of kinematic and semantic data streams. A systemic agentic framework unifies multimodal data ingestion, temporal chunking, and probabilistic synthesis to enable scalable athlete profiling.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference maps athlete profiles to SAI protocols using probabilistic coaching score distributions across form, endurance, and fatigue. Bayesian belief updating on validated kinematic and biomechanical inputs via RAG-enhanced VLMs for probabilistic athlete state estimation.
gse_mapping: Situationally grounded state transitions model athlete form evolution through temporal chunks, enabling dynamic coaching decision trees. Situational reasoning engine employs guardrail agents and smart grid temporal chunking to transition states safely through validated action sequences.

primitives.name: Smart Grid Temporal Chunking

primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \epsilon_{\text{overlap}} < 0.1 \), chunking fails to maintain motion coherence.

reasoning_traces.think: The foundational premise of this work is the recognition that traditional athlete profiling lacks the nuance of human coaching intelligence. This paper proposes an agentic framework integrating computer vision (MediaPipe), vision-language models (Llama-4-scout), and LLM-based reasoning to automate holistic profiling. The framework addresses scalability issues in mass recruitment by introducing a dual-pipeline architecture: one for precise kinematic tracking and another for semantic interpretation. The Smart Grid chunking reduces computational load while maintaining motion fidelity. The LLM-as-a-Judge loop ensures data integrity by validating outputs against known coaching principles. Finally, a dual-persistence RAG pipeline allows semantic querying of athlete profiles. These primitives collectively enable a Bayesian inference system for athlete profiling that aligns with SAI standards, while the GSE layer supports dynamic, situation-aware decision-making based on athlete state transitions. This step mitigates computational waste and prevents hallucinations by filtering out anomalous or irrelevant inputs. Subsequently, the Smart Grid Temporal Chunking strategy addresses the challenge of processing high-definition video through LMMs by sampling at reduced frame rates and condensing frames into composite grid images. This architecture reflects a robust integration of multimodal perception, temporal abstraction, and probabilistic reasoning, forming a scalable foundation for digital coaching intelligence. reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 4 explores the foundational principles of agentic frameworks for athlete profiling, emphasizing temporal sampling dynamics and model selection criteria. The core thesis hinges on optimizing frame rate to prevent context window saturation, which undermines classification accuracy. This aligns with established machine learning theory where increasing input dimensionality without proportional gain in signal-to-noise ratio causes degradation. The paper demonstrates that 2 FPS yields superior performance due to optimal token efficiency, validating a priori hypotheses about attention mechanisms in vision-language models. Furthermore, qualitative analysis reveals that Llama-4-Scout outperforms alternatives in generating semantically coherent feedback, indicating robustness in domain-specific knowledge transfer. The controlled user study reinforces these findings by showing significant improvements in assessment time and expert agreement, underscoring the practical utility of the proposed framework. These insights form a basis for constructing principled sovereign primitives grounded in empirical validation rather than speculative modeling.
